Coach's rule #1: food matters as much as training. Eat every 2–3 hours, protein at every meal, and match your calories to the phase you're in.

Post-workout staple
The Hero Smoothie
Almond milk, 1 banana, dates, almond butter, pinch of salt, ice, chocolate protein powder. The salt helps you hold fluids after training, dates are a natural sweetener, and almond butter provides healthy fat. Works as a full meal replacement on busy days.
6-meal daily structure
6:30am — Meal 1
Power oats + scrambled eggs
1 cup oats, banana, mixed berries, 4 whole eggs. Eggs are the morning protein staple — complete amino profile and fast to prepare.
~600 cal40g protein
9:30am — Meal 2
Grilled chicken + brown rice + veg
200g grilled chicken breast, 3/4 cup brown rice, steamed broccoli. Chicken breast is the workhorse protein — lean, versatile, easy to prep in bulk.
~550 cal50g protein
Pre-workout (45 min before) — Meal 3
Banana + whey protein
1 banana, 30g whey with water or oat milk. Fast carbs for energy, protein to prime muscle protein synthesis before lifting.
~300 cal32g protein
Post-workout (within 30 min) — Meal 4
Hero Smoothie or whey + rice
The Hero Smoothie (above) OR 30g whey + 2 rice cakes with honey. Fast protein + carbs in the recovery window.
~380 cal35g protein
2:30pm — Meal 5
Salmon + sweet potato
180g salmon for omega-3s, 1 medium sweet potato, spinach with olive oil. Rotating fish into your afternoon keeps protein sources varied.
~580 cal45g protein
7:00pm — Meal 6 (big dinner)
Lean beef or chicken thigh + veg
A big dinner after training: 200g lean beef or chicken, roasted vegetables, 1/2 cup rice on training days only.
~650 cal48g protein
9:30pm — Optional Meal 7
Cottage cheese or casein
200g cottage cheese with cinnamon, or casein shake. Slow-digesting protein feeds muscles through the night.
~200 cal25g protein
Coach's rules
Protein first
Hit your protein target every day without fail. Plan nutrition like you plan workouts.
Eat every 2–3 hrs
Frequent meals keep energy stable and muscles in a constant anabolic state.
Carbs around training
Most carbs before and after workouts. Fewer carbs at dinner on rest days.
Cheat meal weekly
One planned cheat meal per week keeps you sane and the plan sustainable. Earn it, enjoy it, move on.
Variety + whole foods
Rotate proteins — chicken, fish, beef, eggs. Don't eat the same thing every day.
3–4L water daily
500ml first thing every morning before coffee. A pinch of salt post-training helps retention.
Your equipment
Supplements
Whey protein
Post-workout and between meals. The easiest way to hit your daily protein target — shakes can replace meals when needed.
Creatine (5g/day)
Most researched supplement available. Take daily with water. Directly increases strength output and muscle volume.
Vitamin D3 + K2
Testosterone support, bone density, muscle function. 2,000–4,000 IU D3 daily with a fat-containing meal.
Omega-3 fish oil
Reduces inflammation and soreness. 2–3g EPA+DHA daily. Eat fatty fish regularly — supplement if diet doesn't match.
Heavy compound lifting builds the base, functional and conditioning work keeps it athletic. That balance — strength plus movement — is exactly what this program builds.

Best for restaurant items — Starbucks, Chuy's, Chick-fil-A, etc. Free tier: 500 searches/day.
